title: As Birds Their Infant Brood Protect
description: As Birds Their Infant Brood Protect in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book I, hymn 72, “Jehovah-Shammah. Ezek 48:33”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: As birds their in-fant brood pro-tect, And spread their wings to shel-ter them; Thus saith the Lord to his e-lect, "So will I guard Je-ru-sa-lem."

lines: As birds their infant brood protect,
And spread their wings to shelter them;
Thus saith the Lord to his elect,
"So will I guard Jerusalem."
And what then is Jerusalem,
This darling object of his care?
Where is its worth in God's esteem,
Who built it? who inhabits there?
Jehovah founded it in blood,
The blood of his incarnate Son;
There dwell the saints, once foes to God,
The sinners, whom he calls his own.
There, though besieged on every side,
Yet much beloved and guarded well;
From age to age they have defied,
The utmost force of earth and hell.
Let earth repent, and hell despair,
This city has a sure defence;
Her name is called, the Lord is there,
And who has pow'r to drive him thence.

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
